While a `herdr --remote` client is attached, your prompt bubble keeps its shape on terminals that cannot show Kitty images, such as foot.

- herdr sends the same screen to every attached client and does not tell apps which terminals they are. A remote client such as foot drops Kitty images, so the rounded corners of a multi-line bubble left empty cells there, which made the top and bottom rows look one cell narrower on each side, and attached image thumbnails left a blank gap
- desk-look now checks for a remote herdr client when a session starts and each time you send a prompt. While one is attached, bubbles draw their corners with glyphs and skip thumbnails. The `└ [Image #N]` line under the bubble still lists the images. Once the remote client leaves, the next prompt brings back the rounded corners and thumbnails, including on bubbles already on screen
- Right after a remote client attaches, the screen keeps the previous look until you send the first prompt. Local-only herdr and terminals outside herdr look the same as before

## Install

```
/plugin install desk-look --marketplace KyongSik-Yoon/cc-desktop-mod
/plugin install desk-asana@cc-desktop-mod
/plugin install desk-slack@cc-desktop-mod
```

Already installed: `/desk-update` (or `claude plugin update desk-look`), then `/reload-plugins`.
